function.name: run_starlark
function.description: Run a Starlark script for computation — sorting, counting, arithmetic, JSON/text transformation, and similar tasks you'd otherwise reach for python -c or a throwaway script for. Starlark is a deterministic, Python-like language (used by Bazel) with no built-in access to the filesystem, network, or other programs, so it is safe to run directly: there is no python or general scripting available, and this is the tool to use instead. The script cannot read files itself — pass any data it needs through "inputs" (read the file first with a file tool), and it cannot write files either — return data through "result" and write it out yourself with file_write_full if needed. Two modules are predeclared: json (json.encode(x), json.decode(s)) and math (math.sqrt, math.floor, math.pow, etc.); everything else is standard Starlark (lists, dicts, string methods, len, range, sorted, comprehensions). Set a global variable named result to whatever value you want returned — it is JSON-encoded automatically; print() output is also captured and included. Execution is capped at a few seconds and a large but finite number of steps, so infinite loops fail cleanly instead of hanging.

script.description: Starlark source to execute. Set a `result` variable to return a value, e.g. "result = sorted(inputs['items'])".

inputs.description: Named values to expose to the script as the `inputs` dict, e.g. {"text": "..."} becomes inputs["text"] in the script. Omit if the script needs no input data.
